sentences.text: Mexico's president gets one term. Six years. Then never again.
Who can vote? Citizens aged 18 with a photo voter card, even online from abroad. Voting is a duty, but there's no fine.
Each race gets its own ballot. Mark one party's logo, or two, if they're in the same alliance.
300 deputies win a district. 200 more are shared by votes, for parties above 3%.
That's the Chamber of Deputies: it makes laws and sets the budget. The 128-member Senate must pass every law too.
There's no prime minister. The president runs the government, and wins with the most votes, no run-off.
And since 2025, Mexicans even elect their judges.
In 2024, Claudia Sheinbaum became the first woman president. Her alliance won 54% of the votes, but 73% of the deputies.
So, should 54% of the votes win 73% of the seats?
